epic.title: Epic #418 wave 5 - bookend gates
epic.intent_and_why: Close the iterative-planning epic's own bookends: the role verifier must know where it is running from, the stop exit must not authorize a next wave, and the archive command text must resolve. Each is a check that today either cannot fail or fails for the wrong reason.

definition_of_done: All six issues are fixed, each behind a gate that fails closed when its tests were never written.

good_enough.mandatory_quality: Every gate closes on a -k selector keyed to a stated test naming contract; a zero-match selector exits 5 and fails the gate.
good_enough.sufficient_evidence: Targeted tests plus the coupled suite at each gate boundary; the full suite at g4.

hard_constraints: scripts/checklist_engine.py and tests/test_checklist_engine.py are crew 4's sole writers this wave
No hooks, no settings.json, no docs/agents/* doctrine promotion
Collateral red in a non-owned file is a float to the Admiral, not a local edit
fixed_decisions: A running process identifies an installed bundle by structure, not by name (launch-order pre-ruling 4)
The -k selectors are the cold critic's BLOCK remedy and are load-bearing, not stylistic

current_wave.objective: Fix the three bookend defects behind gates that cannot close vacuously
exit_criteria: guard_location, guard_mutation, stop_mutation and archive_c2b selectors each collect nonzero and pass
The full suite is green at g4

completed_outcomes.outcome: Fixed. admiral-prelaunch is now decision-aware: a recorded, G2-verified, rendered stop transition packet closes the prelaunch check, while advance and replan are unchanged and repair is still refused. The launch_id relaxation is genuinely conditional, not a blanket loosening.
completed_outcomes.evidence: The stop_boundary and stop_mutation selectors, and the reviewer's own three stop-shortcuts (skip G2 validation, skip the unique-audit-entry match, skip the render) all measured RED at bd56ac8a. Recorded because the FIRST review BLOCKed here: the render shortcut survived green at 57048457, so the mutation test did not cover the leg it claimed to. The gate caught it, not the suite.

completed_outcomes.outcome: Fixed, but NOT as the issue describes. The issue's diagnosis (the literal <branch> token ships unsubstituted) is right about the token and wrong about the consequence: gh never ran at all, because '<' is a shell input redirection under sh -c. The branch is now derived at CHECK time from the existing <repo-root> token, so no new resolver token was needed and scripts/init_work_area.py took a zero-line diff.
completed_outcomes.evidence: The four-state matrix and the always-fails reproduction in wave_evidence, plus test_archive_c2b_derives_the_branch_from_the_real_repository and the archive_mutation leg that reintroduces the literal token.

completed_outcomes.outcome: Fixed, but the issue's SUGGESTED replacement was refused with evidence. Keeping --jq 'length > 0' would exit 0 on an empty list -- a check that cannot fail, inside a wave about checks that cannot fail. The count is compared in the shell instead, so the exit code carries the verdict.
completed_outcomes.evidence: The 0/0/0/0 counterfactual measurement in wave_evidence, and the archive_mutation leg that restores the stdout form and goes red.

completed_outcomes.outcome: Fixed as the SECOND defect of the same postcondition, not merged into #439/#484. Its complaint -- that only an OPEN pull request is accepted, so a merged PR (the strongest evidence the work is reachable) fails -- is a distinct defect from the unsubstituted token, and pre-ruling 5 required both be fixed rather than one. The check now accepts {OPEN, MERGED} while still rejecting CLOSED-unmerged and no-PR. Note the issue's premise is also corrected by the always-fails finding: the shipped check rejected a MERGED PR, but so did it reject an OPEN one.
completed_outcomes.evidence: MERGED exit 0 in the four-state matrix; test_archive_c2b_a_merged_pr_alone_satisfies_the_check; and the archive_mutation leg narrowing back to --state open, which is only discriminating on a MERGED fixture -- verified by the reviewer, who measured that the same mutation on an OPEN fixture is a genuine no-op.

Main checkout (C:/Programs/constellation-skills): no own SKILL.md, parent no CORPUS.json, 0 constellation-*/SKILL.md children -> False. Commander worktree (C:/Programs/constellation-skills-wt/epic418-w5-gates): the same three columns -> False.

wave_evidence.claim: The guard is not a check that cannot fail.
wave_evidence.expected: An unconditionally-permissive guard drives the guard_location tests red.
wave_evidence.observed: Replacing _is_installed_bundle's body with `return True` gives 10 failed / 6 passed / 13 deselected, exit 1 -- red on the decoy test, on both non-installed rows of the matrix, and on four runtime resolution tests. The reviewer measured 9 failed independently before I added an eleventh test. Restored and confirmed by blob OID.
wave_evidence.source: Reviewer's own mutation run, and my own re-run after the post-review fix

wave_evidence.claim: The two-clause structural test does not self-certify.
wave_evidence.expected: A lone constellation-*-named directory carrying its own SKILL.md is NOT an installed bundle when nothing else marks its parent.
wave_evidence.observed: Found by the reviewer and fixed at g1-integrate: _is_skills_root globs constellation-* children of the PARENT, so the candidate satisfied clause 2 by being that child, and the test decayed to the old name test plus a SKILL.md. _is_installed_bundle now passes exclude=path. Removing the exclusion drives the new regression test red on assertFalse(_is_installed_bundle(lonely)) -- a behavioural red, not a signature error.

wave_evidence.expected: The flag beats an otherwise-resolvable root and is reachable from all three modes.
wave_evidence.observed: Passing, including test_guard_location_flag_beats_an_otherwise_resolvable_root and test_guard_location_flag_wins_and_is_reachable_from_all_three_modes. g4-integrate.c2 depends on this flag.

wave_evidence.claim: Both -k selectors collect a nonzero number of tests.
wave_evidence.expected: Nonzero collection, so neither gate closes vacuously.
wave_evidence.observed: guard_location 11 passed / 13 deselected, exit 0. guard_mutation 1 passed / 23 deselected, exit 0. Both run unpiped so the exit code is pytest's own. A bogus selector exits 5 on this machine, confirmed by the reviewer as a discriminating control.

wave_evidence.claim: archive.c2b's reachability verdict rides the exit code and discriminates all four pull-request states.
wave_evidence.expected: no-PR and CLOSED-unmerged nonzero (unreachable); OPEN and MERGED zero (reachable).
wave_evidence.observed: no-PR exit 1, OPEN exit 0, MERGED exit 0, CLOSED-unmerged exit 1, with EMPTY stdout in all four -- so nothing rides on printed text. Measured twice independently: by the Commander against four real branches on the live gh, and offline by the implementer and again by the reviewer through a PATH stub running the command text extracted from the shipped template. The three measurements agree.
wave_evidence.source: Live gh (Commander) + stubbed shell at g3-implement, g3-review pass 1 and pass 2

wave_evidence.claim: The SHIPPED archive.c2b was an always-fails check, not an open-PR-only check. #439, #484 and #446 all describe its behaviour wrongly.
wave_evidence.expected: If the issues were right, the old text would exit 0 on an OPEN pull request and nonzero on the other three.
wave_evidence.observed: The old text exits 1 in ALL FOUR states with `bash: line 1: branch: No such file or directory`. The engine runs check text through sh -c, where the unquoted '<' in `--head <branch>' is an INPUT REDIRECTION, so gh was never invoked at all. It passed no-PR and CLOSED-unmerged for entirely the wrong reason. Reproduced independently by the implementer and by the reviewer.
wave_evidence.source: Direct shell runs at g3-implement and g3-review

wave_evidence.claim: Adopting the replacement #484 suggests would convert a check that cannot pass into one that cannot fail.
wave_evidence.expected: If --jq 'length > 0' carried the verdict, an empty list would exit nonzero.
wave_evidence.observed: #484's form exits 0/0/0/0 across all four states. gh --jq prints `true` or `false` and exits 0 either way; a command condition's verdict is its EXIT CODE and stdout is discarded (docs/CHECKLIST_SCHEMA.md). The count is therefore compared IN THE SHELL. Measured by the Commander on live gh and by the reviewer offline.

wave_evidence.claim: The g3 test harness itself could have gone vacuous, and did not, because the reviewer measured it.
wave_evidence.expected: A stub that models the shipped check should refuse any shape it does not model.
wave_evidence.observed: The first stub required --head, --state and --json but rejected nothing EXTRA, so `--repo someone/else` and `--limit 100` were answered silently and read exactly like the baseline -- a future check could have queried the wrong repository with the whole four-state matrix green. Reviewer BLOCKed on it; repaired at 84d1e998 by whitelisting the four modelled flags. Load-bearing confirmed by deleting the guard again: exactly the two new legs go red. Reviewer then probed 21 flag SHAPES (combined-form, short flags, positionals, missing values, adversarial values, unicode lookalikes) and all refuse.
wave_evidence.source: g3-review pass 1 BLOCK, rework 84d1e998, g3-review pass 2 APPROVE
